newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe shares continue strong on local buying.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe shares continue strong on local buying.

text.p: Zimbabwean shares continued their strong run on Wednesday, driven mainly by local institutional buying, brokers said.
"As we predicted, the correction seems to be temporary... The market is looking good and we hope it will stay that way provided a lot of things come together," one broker said.
He was referring to marekt hopes that annual inflation -- which fell to 17.7 percent in August from 22 percent in July -- would keep tracking down.

The 57-share industrial index powered 153.17 points up -- a rise of 2.3 percent -- close Wednesday at 6.919.62, pushed up largely by blue-chip conglomerate Delta's 150-cent jump to 3,150, and merchant bankers FMB as well as publishing group Zimpapers' 100-cent gains to 3,400 and 1,400 respectively.

Agricultural investor Chemco rose 75 cents to 1,100, cement producer Porthold gained 50 cents to 1,250, 25-cent climbs were recorded in timber producer Border at 1,275, tobacco firm TSL added 20 cents to 530 while packaging firm Hunyani and brick-maker and construction firm Mash put on 15 cents each to 395 and 150 respectively.

Minings were also active and largely firmer with gains recorded in gold producers Falgold which put on five cents to 175, Falcon which added 100 cents to 1,800 and Ashanti which rose 300 cents to 15,300. Wankie slipped two cents to 348.
The seven-counter mining index rose 21.58 points to 1,346.79.
